gbm_population_evidence.quote: Patients must have histologically or cytologically confirmed glioblastoma(WHO 2021).

candidate_evidence.quote: NRG-103 is an oncolytic virus, which can kill GBM cells via three manners.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Patients have experienced recurrence (RANO 2.0) after previous anti-tumor treatments, including the recurrent tumor has been surgically removed and an Ommaya reservoir has been placed inside the tumor cavity.

role_evidence.quote: NRG-103 is an oncolytic virus, which can kill GBM cells via three manners.

agents.drug_class_hint: NRG-103, genetically modified oncolytic adenovirus expressing two trans-differentiation transcription factors (gene therapy)
agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: the two transcription factors expressed on NRG-103 can efficiently transdifferentiate residual GBM tumor cells into non tumor like neuronal cells, in order to achieve the goal of delaying tumor recurrence and long-term survival.

coder_notes: Single-arm EARLY_PHASE1 oncolytic adenovirus / gene therapy study; no pharmacological candidate. Dexamethasone is mentioned only as stable background dose in eligibility, not a registered intervention, so not listed.
